Swift's two-phase initializer rule ordinarily requires an explicit delegating call before an initializer returns, but for a designated initializer whose superclass (NSObject here) has a no-argument initializer, the compiler synthesizes that call itself when the source omits it -- there is nothing left for the deleted statement to do that the compiler was not already going to do. No test can distinguish the two forms because the compiled program is the same program either way.
